sentences.zh: 自己有90%的存活几率时糟糕得多，尽管这是同一种治疗方案。

sentences.en: And so I think those are some of the biggest errors that people make.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 我们往往会纠结于消极的一面。

sentences.zh: 我们往往会纠结于消极的一面，但我们也往往会执着于信息呈现出来的形式而不去改变它。

sentences.en: So if they're given, if they're told about a treatment that has, where they have a 10% chance of dying, they're going to feel much worse than if they're told that
sentences.zh: 通过改变信息，你可以获得更有意义的信息。

sentences.en: they would have a 90% chance of survival, even though it's the same treatment.
sentences.zh: 你能够理解摆在你面前的更复杂的一系列信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 不仅是你最有可能存活，你实际上也可能会死。

sentences.en: We tend to latch on to the negative.
sentences.zh: 通过进行这种转换，你可以更深入地理解这一点。

sentences.en: We tend to latch on to the negative, but we also tend to latch on to information in the form it's given and without changing it.

sentences.zh: 概率的概念呢？

sentences.en: You get to understand the more complex set of information that's in front of you.
sentences.zh: 概率的概念呢？

sentences.zh: 概率的概念呢？

sentences.en: And by doing that transformation, you understand that in a deeper way.
sentences.zh: 概率的概念呢？

sentences.zh: 大家对这个概念的理解程度到底有多深？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I've heard people say, well, you know, everything's 50-50, either it will or it won't.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到有人说，嗯，你知道的，凡事都是五五开，要么会发生，要么不会。

sentences.en: And that's not how probability works.
sentences.zh: 但概率可不是这么运作的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 没错，这真的太有意思了。

sentences.en: And it's actually a really interesting problem in medical decision making because to an individual person, that is true.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上是医疗决策中一个非常有趣的问题，因为对于个人而言，事实确实如此。

sentences.en: It's going to happen to me or it's not going to happen to me.
sentences.zh: 这件事要么会发生在我身上，要么不会发生在我身上。

sentences.en: But if you take a step back and you look at a population of people that's similar to that person, then you can get to predicted likelihood.
sentences.zh: 但如果你退一步，去看一个与该人类似的人群，你就能得出预测的可能性。

sentences.en: So, the predicted likelihood that a medication will help you, for example.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，例如，某种药物对你起作用的预测概率。

sentences.en: And people are not very good with probabilities.
sentences.zh: 人们对概率其实并不太敏感。

sentences.en: It's one of the types of math that we tend to have the most problems with.
sentences.zh: 这是我们往往最感到头疼的数学类型之一。

sentences.en: And in fact, most objective numeracy tests deal with probabilistic kinds of information because they tend to be
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数客观的算术能力测试都涉及概率类型的信息，因为它们往往

sentences.en: harder and probabilities are important in a lot of everyday life events.
sentences.zh: 更难，而且概率在许多日常生活事件中非常重要。

sentences.en: You've done research that's looked at how numeracy affects people's health outcomes, their financial outcomes, and other aspects of life.
sentences.zh: 你曾做过研究，探讨算术能力如何影响人们的健康结果、财务结果以及生活的其他方面。

sentences.en: What are the consequences in a day-to-day area of innumeracy?
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中，缺乏算术能力会带来什么后果？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, we actually kind of already started one of those.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们其实已经开始讨论其中一点了。

sentences.en: So, one of the ways that numeracy seems to have impact on people's lives has to do with their ability to make good decisions.
sentences.zh: 算术能力似乎对人们生活产生影响的途径之一，就与他们做出良好决策的能力有关。

sentences.en: Even though everybody might get the same information, they might be given the exact same choice options, people have those different habits that we started talking about.
sentences.zh: 尽管每个人获得的信息可能完全相同，也可能会被赋予完全相同的选择项，但人们有着我们刚才开始讨论的那些不同习惯。

sentences.en: For someone who's less numerate, numbers are harder, as we were talking about.
sentences.zh: 对于算术能力较弱的人来说，正如我们刚才所讨论的，数字更难处理。

sentences.en: And what research ends up showing is that their decisions end up being more vulnerable to their own emotional reactions, to how information is framed, to compelling
sentences.zh: 研究最终表明，他们的决策更容易受到自身情绪反应的影响，受到信息表述方式的影响，受到引人注目的

sentences.en: stories that they're given or images that they're shown.
sentences.zh: 他们得到的故事或看到的图像的影响。

sentences.en: And what this means when they're judging and deciding is that they will be more vulnerable to the framing effects we talked about.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当他们在进行判断和决策时，他们会更容易受到我们刚才讨论的框架效应的影响。

sentences.en: Or they'll be more vulnerable to using other cognitive shortcuts, heuristic shortcuts that people take.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会更容易陷入使用其他认知捷径、人们常采取的启发式捷径中。

sentences.en: They also may end up being, and in fact, research shows that they'll end up being more susceptible just to how they're feeling in the moment, like their mood states.
sentences.zh: 他们最终也可能——事实上研究表明他们最终会——更容易仅仅受到当下感受的影响，比如他们的情绪状态。

sentences.en: And then, ultimately, studies show that they neglect numbers more.
sentences.zh: 最后，研究表明他们会更多地忽视数字。

sentences.en: Even if they think they're using them, they'll end up neglecting numbers more.
sentences.zh: 即使他们认为自己在运用数字，到头来还是会更多地忽视数字。

sentences.en: The people who are highly numerate have a whole different set of habits.
sentences.zh: 算术能力强的人则有一套完全不同的习惯。

sentences.en: So, they're more likely to seek out numbers.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们更有可能主动寻找数字。

sentences.en: They're more likely to think longer about them, to transform numbers, like we were talking about, and do different calculations.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能对数字进行更长时间的思考、转换数字（正如我们刚才所讨论的），以及进行不同的计算。

sentences.en: They're even more likely to compare numbers and do just other kinds of operations with numbers that help them
sentences.zh: 他们甚至更有可能比较数字，并对数字进行其他种类的运算，这有助于他们

sentences.en: see a number that has meaning, rather than see a number that's dry and feels irrelevant to them.
sentences.zh: 看到有意义的数字，而不是看到枯燥且感觉与自己无关的数字。

sentences.en: So, that's kind of the first way that numeracy has an impact.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是算术能力产生影响的第一种方式。

sentences.en: And that has an impact on sort of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这会对某种程度上的日常生活产生影响。

sentences.en: It's not just that math has to do with STEM education.
sentences.zh: 数学不仅仅与STEM教育有关。

sentences.en: Understanding and being able to use math has to do with the quality of your everyday life.
sentences.zh: 理解并能够使用数学与你日常生活的质量息息相关。

sentences.en: And that then, as you started to mention, that then shows up in some of the consequences that people end up with.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才开始提到的那样，这随后会体现在人们最终遭遇的一些后果中。

sentences.en: And my lab is not the only one one that studies this.
sentences.zh: 而且我的实验室并不是唯一一个研究这个课题的。

sentences.en: One study that we've done in our lab shows that people who are highly numerate make more money.
sentences.zh: 我们在实验室做的一项研究表明，算术能力强的人赚的钱更多。

sentences.en: And so, for each individual problem, extra problem that a highly numerate person solved, they made $4,000 more in annual income after controlling for a whole slew of other
sentences.zh: 因此，算术能力强的人每多解决一个问题，在控制了整整一系列其他

sentences.en: demographics.
sentences.zh: 人口统计学变量后，他们的年收入就会增加4000美元。

sentences.en: People who are more numerate also end up being much wealthier.
sentences.zh: 算术能力更强的人最终也会变得更加富有。

sentences.en: People on top of that, but there's only one study that I know of on this.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，据我所知，这方面的研究只有一项。

sentences.en: But people who are more numerate seem to be more likely to be employed rather than unemployed compared to people who are less numerate.
sentences.zh: 但与算术能力较差的人相比，算术能力较强的人似乎更有可能处于就业状态而非失业状态。

sentences.en: And then you get to health gaps.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要谈谈健康差距。

sentences.en: And there have been a whole bunch of different health gaps that have been studied.
sentences.zh: 人们已经研究了许许多多不同的健康差距。

sentences.en: I'll mention just a couple.
sentences.zh: 我只提其中几个。

sentences.en: People who are less numerate are 40% more likely to have at least one chronic disease.
sentences.zh: 算术能力较差的人患至少一种慢性病的可能性要高出40%。

sentences.en: And they also take 20% more prescription drugs, according to this study.
sentences.zh: 根据这项研究，他们服用的处方药也多出20%。

sentences.en: And all of this is while having less ability to follow complex health regimens that involve numbers, because they're having difficulty with numbers.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切发生的同时，他们遵循涉及数字的复杂健康治疗方案的能力却更低，因为他们在处理数字时遇到了困难。

sentences.en: Now, this is a correlation, right?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这是一种相关性，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not talking causation in this instance.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们谈论的不是因果关系。

sentences.en: For the most part, we're talking correlation.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，我们谈论的是相关性。

sentences.en: So, most of the studies have been done
sentences.zh: 因此，大多数研究都是用

sentences.en: with correlational data.
sentences.zh: 相关性数据完成的。

sentences.en: A lot of them control for other non-numeric aspects of intelligence and for other demographics like education.
sentences.zh: 其中许多研究控制了智力中其他非数字方面的因素，以及教育程度等其他人口统计学变量。

sentences.en: But there's still correlational data.
sentences.zh: 但这些仍然是相关性数据。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right about that.
sentences.zh: 你这一点说得完全正确。

sentences.en: There have been a few studies that have looked at experimentally manipulating numeracy.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究探讨了对算术能力进行实验性干预的情况。

sentences.en: And those have found causal effects on risk perceptions, different kinds of behaviors, financial literacy.
sentences.zh: 这些研究发现了对风险感知、不同种类的行为以及金融素养的因果影响。

sentences.en: So, there's a few studies out there.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实有一些这样的研究。

sentences.en: But it's actually difficult to make a large impact on adult numeracy, unless you put them through a very, very long, like a math course,
sentences.zh: 但要对成年人的算术能力产生重大影响其实很难，除非让他们经历一个非常非常长的数学课程，比如，

sentences.en: unless you put them through sort of a long training course.
sentences.zh: 除非让他们经历某种长期的培训课程。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要进行短暂的休息。

sentences.en: And when we return, we'll talk with Dr. Peters about whether our increasing reliance on technology is making us more or less numerate.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将与彼得斯博士探讨，我们对技术的日益依赖究竟是让我们更具算术能力还是更缺乏算术能力。

sentences.en: Is technology making us more innumerate, or is it helping us be less innumerate?
sentences.zh: 技术是让我们变得更不懂数学，还是在帮助我们不那么不懂数学？

sentences.en: I'm asking just like in a day-to-day fashion, like you go to the grocery store, and if the cashier doesn't see what the change is on the
sentences.zh: 我问的只是一种日常生活中的情况，比如你去杂货店，如果收银员在

sentences.en: register, they have no idea how to make change anymore.
sentences.zh: 收银机上看不出找零是多少，他们就完全不知道该怎么找零了。

sentences.en: I mean, I used to have to do that calculation in my head when I was a checker many years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多年前我做收银员时，必须在脑子里进行这种计算。

sentences.en: So, I'm just astonished that people can't do these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们不会做这些事情，这让我感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I actually had a well-known psychologist actually told me a story once.
sentences.zh: 事实上，曾有一位知名的心理学家给我讲过这样一个故事。

sentences.en: He was at a checkout counter.
sentences.zh: 当时他在收银台前。

sentences.en: Let's say the bill was 75 cents.
sentences.zh: 比方说账单是75美分。

sentences.en: How did that work?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: Basically, he was giving her money so that she would give him back a full dollar.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他当时在给她钱，好让收银员找回他整整一美元。

sentences.en: And she couldn't do that on the fly, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，她当场算不出来。

sentences.en: And so, is technology helping or hurting?
sentences.zh: 那么，技术究竟是在帮忙还是在帮倒忙？

sentences.en: I think it's both.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者皆有。

sentences.en: So, I think it's hurting in the sense that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为它在你说的那种意义上是在帮倒忙。

sentences.en: People are kind of losing that ability to make calculations on the fly.
sentences.zh: 人们某种程度上正在失去那种当场进行计算的能力。

sentences.en: And that kind of thing, I suspect, will make people more vulnerable, even more vulnerable to framing effects, for example.
sentences.zh: 我猜，这种现象会让人们更加脆弱，例如，在面对框架效应时甚至会变得更加脆弱。

sentences.en: Because if you don't do that switch from
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不把

sentences.en: 90% survival to 10% dying, then you're not going to have complete information.
sentences.zh: “90%的生存率”转换为“10%的死亡率”，那么你就无法获得完整的信息。

sentences.en: Or you're not going to be able to figure things out at the cashier, all of those kinds of situations.
sentences.zh: 或者你在收银台前就无法弄清楚状况，所有这些情况都是如此。

sentences.en: I think technology helps in other ways, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为技术在其他方面是有帮助的。

sentences.en: So, technology can be used to help support people.
sentences.zh: 因此，技术可以用来帮助支持人们。

sentences.en: If they're not going to understand the numbers, the technology can be that backup system so they don't get cheated, or so that they better know what the meaning of information is.
sentences.zh: 如果他们看不懂数字，技术就能成为那个后备系统，这样他们就不会被骗，或者能更好地了解信息的含义。

sentences.en: So, for example, in medical decision-making, a lot of researchers and folks in the medical field have worked on decision aids.
sentences.zh: 例如，在医疗决策中，许多研究人员和医疗领域的人士一直在致力于研发决策辅助工具。

sentences.en: And those decision aids are very explicitly intended to help people better understand the
sentences.zh: 而这些决策辅助工具非常明确地旨在帮助人们更好地理解

sentences.en: numbers that underlie one cancer screening option versus another, for example, or one treatment option versus another.
sentences.zh: 例如，某种癌症筛查选项与另一种选项相比，或者某种治疗选项与另一种选项相比，其背后的数字。

sentences.en: And so, the technology also supports.
sentences.zh: 因此，技术同时也提供支持。

sentences.en: So, I'd say it's kind of a two-edged sword.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这算是一把双刃剑。

sentences.en: Now, you've done some research that's looked at people's actual skill and their confidence with numbers and how those two things interact.
sentences.zh: 现在，你做过一些研究，探讨了人们实际的技能、他们对数字的信心以及这两者是如何相互作用的。

sentences.en: What have you found?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I just found this fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以，我发现这太迷人了。

sentences.en: We had started to study objective numeracy kind of early in my career.
sentences.zh: 在我职业生涯的早期，我们就开始研究客观算术能力。

sentences.en: And then along the way, I came across this idea of numeric confidence and realized that it's almost equally important to objective numeracy.
sentences.zh: 然后在研究过程中，我遇到了“数字信心”这个概念，并意识到它几乎与客观算术能力同等重要。

sentences.en: So, we did a set of two studies in one paper that came out in PNAS.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在发表于《美国国家科学院院刊》（PNAS）的一篇论文中做了一组两项研究。

sentences.en: And they're both correlational studies.
sentences.zh: 它们都是相关性研究。

sentences.en: But what we did, one of them was in a financial domain and one was in a medical domain.
sentences.zh: 但我们所做的是，其中一项在金融领域，另一项在医疗领域。

sentences.en: And so, we had access to people's self-reported financial outcomes, whether they had ever carried
sentences.zh: 因此，我们获得了人们自述的财务结果数据，例如他们是否曾经背负过

sentences.en: more than $5,000 in credit card debt, for example, whether they had ever defaulted on their mortgage, whether they had retirement savings.
sentences.zh: 超过5000美元的信用卡债务、是否曾在房贷上违约、是否有退休储蓄。

sentences.en: So, some of the outcomes were positive and some were negative.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些结果是积极的，有些则是消极的。

sentences.en: We transformed it so that everything was about positive outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们对其进行了转换，使所有内容都围绕积极的结果展开。

sentences.en: In other words, so you have not defaulted on your mortgage is a positive outcome.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，“你没有在房贷上违约”就是一个积极的结果。

sentences.en: And then we measured their objective numeracy and we measured their numeric confidence.
sentences.zh: 然后我们测量了他们的客观算术能力，并测量了他们的数字信心。

sentences.en: And what we found, and you can think about it in sort of two different ways.
sentences.zh: 我们所发现的结果，你可以从两种不同的方式来理解。

sentences.en: One thing that we found was that when people are high in numeric confidence, their objective numeracy matters.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的一点是，当人们具有很高的数字信心时，他们的客观算术能力就很重要了。

sentences.en: So, if they're high in numeric confidence and they have high objective numeracy, they do really well in financial outcomes.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他们数字信心高且客观算术能力高，他们的财务结果就会非常好。

sentences.en: But if they're high in numeric confidence and they're actually very low in ability, which does happen, those are
sentences.zh: 但如果他们数字信心很高，而实际能力却非常低（这种情况确实会发生），那么这些就是

sentences.en: the people who do the worSt. And so, when you're high in confidence, it can help you if you have the ability and it helps you to flourish.
sentences.zh: 表现最差的人。因此，当你信心高时，如果你有能力，它能帮助你，助你蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But if you're low in ability, what we think happens is that they go ahead and take charge of their own decisions because they're confident they can do it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能力低下，我们认为发生的情况是：他们依然会掌控自己的决策，因为他们坚信自己能做到。

sentences.en: But while they're confident they can do it, they may be making mistakes because they don't have
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管他们确信自己能做到，他们可能会犯错，因为他们没有

sentences.en: the ability and they may not be catching those mistakes again because they don't have the ability
sentences.zh: 这种能力；而且他们可能又察觉不到这些错误，因为他们没有这种能力；

sentences.en: and they may not be asking for help again because they think they have that ability.
sentences.zh: 并且他们可能也不会寻求帮助，因为他们认为自己具备这种能力。

sentences.en: But then if you look at the people who are low in confidence, this is, I found this fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看那些信心不足的人——我觉得这太迷人了。

sentences.en: Objective ability almost made no difference to their financial outcomes.
sentences.zh: 客观能力对他们的财务结果几乎没有产生任何影响。

sentences.en: Whether they are high or low in objective ability, when they had low confidence, it's like they just didn't step up to the plate.
sentences.zh: 无论他们的客观能力高低，当他们缺乏信心时，就好像他们根本没有走上战场去应对。

sentences.en: They just didn't try to use their numeric abilities.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不尝试去运用自己的数字能力。

sentences.en: And because of that, their financial outcomes were about the same, whether they're low or high in ability.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，无论他们的能力是高是低，他们的财务结果都差不多。

sentences.en: Those were self-reported financial outcomes.
sentences.zh: 那些都是自述的财务结果。

sentences.en: And so, we're also really interested in, can we get to a more real outcome?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们也对一件事很感兴趣：我们能否得出更真实的结果？

sentences.en: Not that those aren't a real outcome, but they're self-reported.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说那些不是真实结果，但它们是自述的。

sentences.en: But I was working with a few rheumatologists at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我正与几位风湿病学家合作。

sentences.en: This is a type of doctor who treats people with things like arthritis, but they also treat people who have lupus.
sentences.zh: 这是一种治疗关节炎等疾病的医生，但他们也治疗患有狼疮的病人。

sentences.en: And lupus is a very serious autoimmune disease that actually involves a lot of numeric processing because they have to figure out how to take medication.
sentences.zh: 狼疮是一种非常严重的自身免疫性疾病，实际上涉及大量的数字处理，因为患者必须弄清楚如何服用药物。

sentences.en: They have to understand the risks and benefits of their medication.
sentences.zh: 他们必须了解药物的风险和收益。

sentences.en: They have to get to doctor's appointment.
sentences.zh: 他们必须按时去进行医生预约。

sentences.en: There's just kind of a whole bunch of little numeric tasks that they have to do on an everyday basis.
sentences.zh: 这其中包含了一大堆他们必须在日常生活中完成的小型数字任务。

sentences.en: And so, we're interested in taking a look at the same hypothesis with them.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有兴趣对他们应用同样的假设进行研究。

sentences.en: And in particular, because if they gave us permission, we would have access into their medical records
sentences.zh: 特别是，如果他们给予我们授权，我们将能够查阅他们的医疗记录，

sentences.en: and we could see how the physician thought they were doing in terms of how active their lupus was.
sentences.zh: 并且我们可以看到医生如何评估他们在狼疮活跃度方面的表现。

sentences.en: And so, we were with two rheumatologists helping out.
sentences.zh: 于是我们在两位风湿病学家的协助下开展了工作。

sentences.en: We actually were able to access a sample of lupus patients who very kindly agreed to do our measures of numeracy and numeric confidence.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上成功获取了一组狼疮患者样本，他们非常善意地同意参与我们的算术能力和数字信心测量。

sentences.en: And they very kindly allowed us access into their medical records.
sentences.zh: 他们非常慷慨地允许我们查阅他们的医疗记录。

sentences.en: And we found the same result.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了同样的结果。

sentences.en: The people who were low in confidence, their ability didn't make a difference.
sentences.zh: 对于那些信心不足的人来说，他们的能力并没有带来差异。

sentences.en: But if they were very high in numeric confidence, if they were high in ability, they did great.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们对数字非常有信心，且能力也很高，他们就表现得极好。

sentences.en: Their health was doing great.
sentences.zh: 他们的健康状况极佳。

sentences.en: But if they were high in confidence, but they were low in ability, those are the people
sentences.zh: 但如果他们信心很高，但能力却很低，这部分人

sentences.en: who were actually doing the worSt. Their disease activity was the highest, and they were at most risk for long-term damage.
sentences.zh: 其实表现得最糟。他们的疾病活动度最高，面临的长期损伤风险也最大。

sentences.en: What can people do to improve their numeracy?
sentences.zh: 人们可以做些什么来提高他们的算术能力？

sentences.en: There's a number of things people can do.
sentences.zh: 人们可以做很多事情。

sentences.en: The first one has to do with what we were just talking about, that interesting relationship between objective ability and numeric confidence.
sentences.zh: 第一件事与我们刚才讨论的内容有关，即客观能力与数字信心之间那种有趣的联系。

sentences.en: The first thing people can do is figure out who they are as a math person.
sentences.zh: 人们可以做的第一件事是弄清楚自己作为一个“擅长数学的人”是怎样的定位。

sentences.en: Because believing you're not skilled when you really are can hurt you.
sentences.zh: 因为当你明明很有技巧却认为自己不行时，这会伤害到你。

sentences.en: Because you're not doing as well.
sentences.zh: 因为你会表现得不够好。

sentences.en: You're not taking advantage of the skills that you actually have.
sentences.zh: 你没有充分利用自己实际拥有的技能。

sentences.en: And so people need to be open to the possibility that they might be good at math so that they're more likely to use numbers in these everyday kinds of situations that we're
sentences.zh: 因此，人们需要对他们可能擅长数学这种可能性保持开放的心态，这样他们就更有可能在我们正在讨论的

sentences.en: talking about.
sentences.zh: 这种日常情况下使用数字。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, believing that you're skilled at math when you really don't have those kind of math skills, that can really hurt you.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，如果你实际上并不具备那种数学能力，却认为自己精通数学，这真的会害了你。

sentences.en: So encouraging people to figure out where they are.
sentences.zh: 所以，鼓励人们去弄清楚自己的水平在哪里。

sentences.en: Like, who am I as a math person?
sentences.zh: 比如，作为一个懂数学的人，我是谁？

sentences.en: How can I match my level of numeric confidence with the level of ability that I actually have can really help?
sentences.zh: 我如何将自己对数字的自信心与我实际具备的能力水平匹配起来，这真的有帮助吗？

sentences.en: It means that you'll ask for help if you need it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果需要的话你会主动寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And maybe you'll try harder if you really have the skill, but you're just not confident about it.
sentences.zh: 也许如果你真的有这个能力，只是缺乏信心，你会去更加努力地尝试。

sentences.en: Something else, people can become more numerate.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，人们的数字素养是可以提高的。

sentences.en: It takes practice.
sentences.zh: 这需要练习。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of research on this.
sentences.zh: 关于这方面的研究并不多。

sentences.en: So a little bit, this has to be taken with a little bit of a grain of salt.
sentences.zh: 所以对于这一点，大家需要对它持有些许保留态度。

sentences.en: But people can take math classes.
sentences.zh: 不过人们可以去上数学课。

sentences.en: That would be the hardest thing.
sentences.zh: 那将会是最难的部分。

sentences.en: And that kind of practice would likely matter.
sentences.zh: 这种练习很可能会发挥作用。

sentences.en: We have done some research that suggests that just practicing in an easier way can help.
sentences.zh: 我们做过的一些研究表明，仅仅通过一种更简单的方式进行练习就能有所帮助。

sentences.en: You don't have to practice with particularly difficult math.
sentences.zh: 你不需要练习特别困难的数学。

sentences.en: But if you practice with simple math, like adding and subtracting numbers, practice by estimating the answers.
sentences.zh: 但如果你练习简单的数学，比如加减法，可以通过估算答案来进行练习。

sentences.en: You first have to estimate the answer before you see it, because you have to get feedback about whether you're right or wrong so that you can actually learn.
sentences.zh: 你在看到答案之前必须先估算出答案，因为你必须获得关于自己是对还是错的反馈，这样你才能真正学到东西。

sentences.en: It turns out that learning requires knowing what you've done correctly and what you've done incorrectly so you can do better the next time.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，学习需要了解你做对了什么、做错了什么，这样你下次才能做得更好。

sentences.en: But our research shows that even doing this in about six sessions of about 30 to 45 minutes, if I remember correctly, this can improve people's objective numeracy.
sentences.zh: 但我们的研究表明，如果我没记错的话，即使只是进行大约六次、每次30到45分钟的这种练习，也能提高人们的客观数字素养。

sentences.en: And it actually did improve the consistency with which people perceived risks.
sentences.zh: 它实际上确实提高了人们感知风险的一致性。

sentences.en: So we know that that helps.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这确实有帮助。

sentences.en: We need more research on it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要对这方面进行更多的研究。

sentences.en: But again, it is hard to manipulate numeracy among adults.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，要操纵成年人的数字素养是很难的。

sentences.en: Another thing, and then just sort of a long series of studies in my lab and others, suggests that that idea of developing good number habits may be important.
sentences.zh: 另一件事，根据我和其他人实验室里的一系列研究表明，培养良好数字习惯这个想法可能很重要。

sentences.en: And so people should pay attention to the numbers in their lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们应该关注生活中的数字。

sentences.en: Try not just to read over them.
sentences.zh: 尽量不要只是粗略地扫一眼。

sentences.en: Develop good net number habits by spending more time, by transforming and calculating numbers, by comparing numbers.
sentences.zh: 通过花更多时间、通过转换和计算数字、通过比较数字来养成良好的数字习惯。

sentences.en: Sometimes that makes all the difference.
sentences.zh: 有时这会带来截然不同的结果。

sentences.en: If you know that how likely some treatment is to help you, take a look at some other plausible treatment and compare it and see which one might actually offer you more benefit.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道某种治疗方法对你有多大帮助，去看一看其他貌似可行的治疗方法并进行比较，看看哪一种实际上能为你提供更多益处。

sentences.en: That'll help you derive more affective or emotional meaning from the numbers.
sentences.zh: 这会帮助你从数字中获得更多情感或心理上的意义。

sentences.en: And then the last thing kind of gets back to that technology question that you mentioned, Kim.
sentences.zh: 最后一点有点回到你之前提到的那个技术问题上了，金。

sentences.en: And the idea is to advocate for yourself if you don't understand some number.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，如果你看不懂某个数字，就要为自己发声。

sentences.en: Or if the person didn't provide a number and you feel like it might be helpful,
sentences.zh: 或者如果对方没有提供数字而你觉得这可能会有帮助，

sentences.en: you can ask like a physician, how statistically likely is something?
sentences.zh: 你可以问医生，某件事在统计学上的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: What is the probability of something happening?
sentences.zh: 某事发生的概率是多少？

sentences.en: Or if you're given too many options or too much information, you can ask a professional to simplify the information so that to whatever is the most important information in
sentences.zh: 或者如果你被给予了太多选项或太多信息，你可以请专业人士将信息简化，

sentences.en: their view.
sentences.zh: 简化为他们认为最核心的信息。

sentences.en: And by doing that, people actually will understand more.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，人们实际上会理解得更多。

sentences.en: Sometimes less can be more.
sentences.zh: 有时少即是多。

sentences.en: What about the people who need to convey numerical information, whether that's doctors talking to
sentences.zh: 那么对于那些需要传达数字信息的人来说呢，无论是医生与

sentences.en: patients or maybe journalists explaining economic data, scientists who are trying to explain climate risk?
sentences.zh: 患者交谈，还是记者解释经济数据，或者是试图解释气候风险的科学家？

sentences.en: How can they help people better understand the numbers they're putting out there so that we can make better decisions?
sentences.zh: 他们怎样才能帮助人们更好地理解他们发布的数据，以便我们能够做出更好的决策？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a series of recommendations that I would make from my lab and communicators will often make.
sentences.zh: 因此，我所在的实验室以及沟通专家们通常会提出一系列建议。

sentences.en: The first one is to have a communication goal.
sentences.zh: 第一点是确立一个沟通目标。

sentences.en: And that sounds kind of silly in some ways.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面听起来这似乎有点傻。

sentences.en: But I've been in all kinds of interviews where I'm sitting in like on a doctor's
sentences.zh: 但我参加过各种各样的采访，我坐在那里旁听医生

sentences.en: visit with a patient or a physical therapist appointment with parents of a child who's not doing well.
sentences.zh: 与患者的会诊，或者是物理治疗师与病情不佳的儿童家长的预约面谈。

sentences.en: And they often go in with this mound of information that they pick up and they put down in front of the patient.
sentences.zh: 他们进去时往往带着一堆信息，拿出来摆在患者面前。

sentences.en: And without really thinking about, what does this person really need to know?
sentences.zh: 却没有真正去思考：这个人真正需要知道的是什么？

sentences.en: How can I facilitate how they understand?
sentences.zh: 我该如何促进他们的理解？

sentences.en: If you sit back and think first about what a communication goal is, that means that you can actually strategically choose what information to show.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐下来首先思考沟通目标是什么，这意味着你可以有策略地选择展示哪些信息。

sentences.en: And then think about, again, strategically, how might I show it?
sentences.zh: 然后同样有策略地思考：我该如何展示这些信息？

sentences.en: And then we get to the kinds of research that I do, which has to do with how do you format information?
sentences.zh: 接下来就到了我所从事的研究类型，这与如何排版和格式化信息有关。

sentences.en: What kinds of information might you show?
sentences.zh: 你可能会展示什么样的信息？

sentences.en: And one of the first recommendations that I always have is to communicate with numbers, not only words.
sentences.zh: 我总是给出的第一个建议是：用数字沟通，而不仅仅是文字。

sentences.en: So people, there's this funny thing that happens where people often prefer communicating with verbal terms like common and unlikely, but people actually kind of prefer
sentences.zh: 所以人们身上会发生一件很有趣的事，大家通常更喜欢用诸如“常见”和“不太可能”这样的口头词汇来沟通，但实际上人们其实更倾向于

sentences.en: getting numbers.
sentences.zh: 获取数字。

sentences.en: And not only do they prefer getting numbers, but they also better understand risks and they can react appropriately when numbers are discussed.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅更喜欢获取数字，当讨论数字时，他们也能更好地理解风险并做出适当的反应。

sentences.en: So long as the numbers aren't too difficult.
sentences.zh: 只要这些数字不是太难。

sentences.en: You don't want to provide too many numbers.
sentences.zh: 你不会希望提供太多的数字。

sentences.en: But what ends up happening when you provide numeric information is not only do people understand better, which helps to support informed consent
sentences.zh: 但当你提供数字信息时，最终发生的情况不仅是人们理解得更好（这有助于支持知情同意

sentences.en: processes and other things like that.
sentences.zh: 流程以及其他类似的事情），

sentences.en: But they're also just the mere presence of numbers seems to increase people's trust in the message and their perceptions of the expertise of the messenger.
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅是数字的存在，似乎就能增加人们对信息的信任度以及对信使专业性的认知。

sentences.en: And on social media, for example, people are more likely to share numbers that include numeric information compared to this exact same message minus the numbers.
sentences.zh: 例如，在社交媒体上，与完全相同但删去数字的消息相比，人们更有可能分享包含数字信息的内容。

sentences.en: So that's one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一点。

sentences.en: Communicate with numbers.
sentences.zh: 用数字进行沟通。

sentences.en: But you do have to make those numbers more manageable.
sentences.zh: 但你确实必须让这些数字更容易处理。

sentences.en: And there's sort of two ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 这里有两种方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: One is to provide less information.
sentences.zh: 一是提供较少的信息。

sentences.en: So remember that communication goal.
sentences.zh: 所以要记住那个沟通目标。

sentences.en: You want to provide information that helps to meet the goal, but not more information than that if you can help it.
sentences.zh: 你想提供有助于达成目标的信息，如果可以的话，不要提供超出范围的更多信息。

sentences.en: Because more information means just a greater likelihood of losing somebody along the way.
sentences.zh: 因为更多信息意味着在沟通中途失去某个人的可能性更大。

sentences.en: With less information, people do understand more.
sentences.zh: 信息越少，人们确实理解得越多。

sentences.en: So you want to avoid cognitive overload.
sentences.zh: 所以你要避免认知过载。

sentences.en: The other part of making numbers more manageable is do the math for people.
sentences.zh: 使数字更容易处理的另一个方法是替人们算好账。

sentences.en: We often give people information where they have to do a little math and you'll lose so many people along the way.
sentences.zh: 我们经常给人们提供需要他们自己动脑算一下的信息，而这会让你在半路上失去很多听众。

sentences.en: Another thing would be to make numbers more meaningful.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是让数字更有意义。

sentences.en: You can provide context like we talked about this a little bit before too.
sentences.zh: 你可以提供背景信息，就像我们之前稍微讨论过的那样。

sentences.en: If you talk about
sentences.zh: 如果你谈到

sentences.en: 93% of patients will survive from treatment A, maybe you also want to give them a comparison.
sentences.zh: 93%的患者在接受治疗A后会存活，也许你还想给他们提供一个对比。

sentences.en: This is compared to 99% of people who would survive with treatment B.
sentences.zh: 这与接受治疗B能存活的99%的人相比如何。

sentences.en: And by having that comparison, people can draw their own meaning.
sentences.zh: 通过这种对比，人们可以从中得出自己的意义。

sentences.en: What are some of the other things?
sentences.zh: 还有哪些其他方面？

sentences.en: This goes back to more general communication advice from the literature.
sentences.zh: 这回到了文献中更一般的沟通建议上。

sentences.en: We often want to inform people and we want to help them better understand a situation that they're in so that they can make their own decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们通常希望告知人们信息，并希望帮助他们更好地理解他们所处的境况，以便他们能够做出自己的决定。

sentences.en: And you don't want to overwhelm them like we were saying.
sentences.zh: 正如我们刚才所说，你不想让他们感到不知所措。

sentences.en: But in the end, we also often want to tell people what are the possible solutions here?
sentences.zh: 但最终，我们通常也希望告诉人们：这里有哪些可能的解决方案？

sentences.en: And you want those solutions to be something that people think will work and that they're confident that they themselves can do.
sentences.zh: 你希望这些解决方案是人们认为可行、并且他们自己有信心能够做到的。

sentences.en: And so that kind of furnishing of feasible solutions is really important.
sentences.zh: 因此，提供这种切实可行的解决方案非常重要。

sentences.en: And we think about that a lot when it comes to communicating about hazards.
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑传达有关灾害的信息时，我们会经常思考这一点。

sentences.en: So if you're communicating about earthquakes, for example, in the Pacific Northwest, you want to
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在传达有关太平洋西北地区地震的信息时，你不仅要

sentences.en: make sure not only that you communicate about the risk of an earthquake and what might happen, what the
sentences.zh: 确保传达地震的风险以及可能发生的情况、

sentences.en: likelihood might be, what those consequences might be, but you also want to tell people what can I do about it?
sentences.zh: 可能性有多大、后果可能是什么，还要告诉人们：我能为此做些什么？

sentences.en: What can I do?
sentences.zh: 我能做点什么？

sentences.en: What can I do that will work?
sentences.zh: 我能做什么才管用？

sentences.en: And what can I do that I'm confident that I can actually do?
sentences.zh: 我能做什么并且有信心自己真的能做到？

sentences.en: And so those are kind of some of the general things that I think about when it comes to
sentences.zh: 因此，这些是我在考虑

sentences.en: communicating numbers, but also going beyond numbers to the idea that we're communicating to help people's lives.
sentences.zh: 传达数字时想到的一些普遍问题，同时也超越了数字本身，延伸到我们通过沟通来改善人们生活的理念。

sentences.en: So you want to go beyond the numbers to things like furnishing solutions that are doable for people.
sentences.zh: 所以你要超越数字，深入到诸如为人们提供切实可行的解决方案之类的事情中去。

sentences.en: Oh, that makes perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 哦，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: So what are the big questions you still want to answer?
sentences.zh: 那么，你仍然想解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: What are you working on right now?
sentences.zh: 你目前正在进行什么研究？

sentences.en: Oh, you know, we are still looking a bit at the mere presence of numbers.
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道的，我们仍在关注数字本身的纯粹存在。

sentences.en: You know, I have to admit, I come from an engineering background originally.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不得不承认，我最初是工程学背景出身。

sentences.en: And so I'm a little bit of a geek when it comes to numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以一谈到数字，我有点像个极客。

sentences.en: And so I just, I personally just find it fascinating that the mere presence of numbers can change how much people trust, how much people think someone's an expert.
sentences.zh: 因此我个人只是觉得，仅仅是数字的存在就能改变人们信任的程度以及认为某人是专家的程度，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And I'm curious about why.
sentences.zh: 我也很好奇这是为什么。

sentences.en: So we're sort of delving into that a bit more.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在对此进行更深入的探讨。

sentences.en: We just in the past probably a year or two have been looking more into how can we communicate more effectively about hazards that people face.
sentences.zh: 在过去差不多一两年里，我们一直在深入研究如何才能更有效地传达人们所面临的灾害信息。

sentences.en: And those are the earthquakes and the wildfires.
sentences.zh: 这些灾害就是地震和野火。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is I love doing psychological science.
sentences.zh: 这样做的原因是，我热爱心理科学。

sentences.en: I love the brain candy of psychological science.
sentences.zh: 我热爱心理科学带来的精神大餐。

sentences.en: It's just really interesting to find out how the human mind works, but I also want it to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚人类思维是如何运作的真的很有趣，但我也希望它能产生影响。

sentences.en: And so I want to make a difference in people's lives and hopefully, you know, help people to better understand something that's important
sentences.zh: 因此，我想对人们的生活产生影响，希望，你知道的，能帮助人们更好地理解对他们而言重要的事情，

sentences.en: to them and that will help just help improve the quality of their life.
sentences.zh: 并且这有助于提高他们的生活质量。

sentences.en: And so that's why we've gone into some of the hazards research, because I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们涉足灾害研究，因为我认为这很重要。
